name: What type of drywall is best for a basement finish?

mainEntity.name: What type of drywall is best for a basement finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: Moisture-resistant drywall, commonly called green board or purple board, is generally recommended for basement spaces. Basements naturally hold more humidity than above-ground levels, and standard drywall can absorb that moisture, risking mold growth. Areas near basement bathrooms, laundry setups, or exterior foundation walls benefit most from moisture- and mold-resistant panels. For utility rooms or furnace enclosures, fire-rated Type X drywall may also be required by local building practices. A contractor can evaluate your basement's specific moisture levels and framing to recommend the right combination of standard, mold-resistant, or fire-rated boards.
acceptedAnswer.description: Moisture- and mold-resistant drywall is best for basements due to natural humidity, while fire-rated drywall is often needed near utility rooms.
